# Kuntinījātaka (Ja 343)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Kuntinījātaka* (Ja 343) is a narrative belonging to the Jātaka collection of the Pali canon. According to its traditional introductory account, the Buddha delivered the story while residing at Jetavana concerning a heron that dwelled in the house of the king of Kosala, opening with the verse line "Long I held". In the conclusion (*samodhāna*) preserved in the commentary edited by V. Fausböll, the female bird (*sakuṇikā*) explains that she can no longer reside there, takes leave of the king, and flies away to the Himalayas [Fausböll 1883]. The Master then resolves the birth story by identifying that the heron of that time was the heron of the present, while the Bodhisatta was the king of Bārāṇasī [Fausböll 1883]. Variant manuscript readings documented in Fausböll's edition attest to spelling variations between *kuntanī* and *kuntinī* [Fausböll 1883].
